questions.q: '___ it rained heavily, the match continued.' because or although?
questions.a: 'although' — the match continuing DESPITE rain is concession, not causation. A wrong answer 'because' makes rain the reason the match continued — a logic-flip.

questions.q: Fix the punctuation: 'When the bell rang the students rushed out.'
questions.a: 'When the bell rang, the students rushed out' — a fronted dependent clause needs its comma. A wrong answer adding it after 'students' breaks the wrong place.

questions.q: 'I will wait ___ you return.' — until or unless?
questions.a: 'until' — waiting up to the moment of return (time-limit). 'Unless' would mean 'if you don't return' — a wrong answer swaps condition for time-limit.

questions.q: ______ conjunctions — because, although, when, while, if, since, unless, until — create dependent clauses that lean on a main clause.
Fill in the blank: ______ conjunctions — because, although, when, while, if, since, unless, until — create dependent clauses that lean on a main clause.
Fill in the blank: The leaning-words map: although = 'yes, BUT anyway' (______); unless = 'if not' (negative condition); until = 'up to the moment' (limit).
What is Subordinating conjunctions? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Subordinating conjunctions — because, although, when, while, if, since, unless, until — create dependent clauses that lean on a main clause.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Subordinating conjunctions?
questions.a: Students use 'because' for every logic ('because it rained, we stayed home' is right; but 'because it rained, we still played' is a logic-flip — needs 'although').

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student selects the subordinator matching the intended logic, places the dependent clause correctly (front position needs a comma), and distinguishes since-time from since-reason.
